question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of severe, acute, right leg pain for 2 hours. The patient's symptoms started suddenly while he was doing household chores. He has no history of leg pain at rest or with exertion. Yesterday, he returned home after a 6-hour bus ride from his grandson's home. He has hypertension treated with ramipril. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 105/min and irregular, and blood pressure is 146/92 mm Hg. The right lower extremity is cool and tender to touch. A photograph of the limb is shown. Femoral pulses are palpable bilaterally; popliteal and pedal pulses are decreased on the right side. Sensation to pinprick and light touch and muscle strength are decreased in the right lower extremity. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the underlying source of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man" -> "recent long bus ride" -> "prolonged immobility" -> "increased risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)" -> "acute onset of severe leg pain" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased popliteal and pedal pulses on the right side" -> "Doppler ultrasonography of the legs to assess blood flow and detect clots" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Irregular pulse at 105/min" -> "potential atrial fibrillation" -> "risk of cardiac emboli formation" -> "embolus may travel to peripheral arteries" -> "sudden severe leg pain due to arterial blockage" -> "Echocardiography to evaluate for atrial fibrillation and cardiac source of emboli" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Decreased sensation and muscle strength in right lower extremity" -> "possible nerve compression or damage" -> "acute onset suggests vascular cause rather than chronic compression" -> "Digital subtraction angiography to visualize arterial blockages" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Cool, tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased peripheral pulses" -> "possible arterial occlusion" -> "Digital subtraction angiography to confirm and locate arterial occlusion" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Decreased popliteal and pedal pulses" -> "vascular compromise in right leg" -> "Doppler ultrasonography to check for arterial or venous occlusion" -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation of acute, severe right leg pain following prolonged immobility, along with clinical signs such as decreased pulses and cool extremity, strongly suggests deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Doppler ultrasonography of the legs is the recommended diagnostic test to confirm this suspicion, as it is effective in detecting venous clots and aligns with medical consensus and evidence paths linking immobility to DVT and ultrasonography as a diagnostic tool for vascular issues in the limbs.
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history suggest a vascular obstruction in the leg, likely due to DVT or arterial occlusion. Doppler ultrasonography of the legs is the most appropriate diagnostic tool to confirm this, given its effectiveness in detecting blood flow abnormalities and its non-invasive nature. This aligns with medical consensus for such clinical presentations.
